input.scenario_context: The Bellgrove Arts Fund normally sends award decisions through its applicant portal. A new email displays the sender name 'Bellgrove Arts Fund' and says a grant is waiting. The full sender address is not shown in the training image. The learner has not opened any link.

verification_steps: Check the grant decision by independently opening the saved Bellgrove applicant portal.

input.scenario_context: A Maple Quay ceramics studio text demands a deposit within ten minutes to retain a class seat. A suspicious link appears in the text. Only pressure recognition and independent booking verification are configured for this exercise.
input.conversation_history:
Tutor: What is the message trying to make you do?
Learner: The ten-minute deadline is trying to rush me.
Tutor: How can you check your booking without the text link?
Learner: I will use the studio's number on my existing class receipt.
input.student_message: I called the number on my old class receipt instead of using the message. They confirmed my booking is unchanged.

detection_areas: Recognize the short deadline as pressure to act before checking.
verification_steps: Verify the booking through a contact recorded on an existing trusted receipt, without using the message link.

input.scenario_context: A Pine Lantern museum membership email addresses the learner by full name and membership number. The message asks the learner to verify their account through an unfamiliar link. The learner can contact the museum using their physical membership card.
input.conversation_history:
Tutor: Does knowing your membership number establish who sent the message?
Learner: No. Someone could get my details, so I need to contact the museum using my card.
Tutor: Now consider that it also uses your full name. Does adding your name prove it came from the museum?
input.student_message: Actually, having both my name and membership number proves the sender is the museum.

detection_areas: Possession of personal details does not prove a message sender's identity.
verification_steps: Contact the museum using the number on the physical membership card.

input.scenario_context: An invitation claiming to be from Ridgebrook Debate Society offers a finalist place. It says 'Reply in five minutes' and comes from awards@ridgebrook-debate.example, while the society's known address uses ridgebrookdebate.example. The learner has not clicked anything.

detection_areas: Recognize time pressure.
Compare the exact sender domain with the organization's known domain.

input.scenario_context: The learner is examining a parking-permit renewal email for Cedar Bend College. Its sender address is shown, but no evidence has established whether the message is legitimate. No earlier participation record is available.
